knowledge:
- key_parameters: x=Numeric vector of temperatures (independent variable) ;; y=Numeric vector of relative abundances (dependent variable) ;; id=Character vector of unique protein identifiers ;; groupsNull=Grouping factor for the null model (typically NULL to fit a single curve across all conditions) ;; groupsAlt=Grouping factor for the alternative model (typically the treatment/compound concentration) ;; dfType=Character string, either "theoretical" (assumes iid residuals) or "empirical" (estimates degrees of freedom from the data, highly recommended to avoid anti-conservative p-values) ;; BPPARAM=BiocParallel parameter object (e.g., BiocParallel::SerialParam()) for parallel execution
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation.
- when_to_use: When analyzing thermal proteome profiling (TPP) or similar temperature-range relative abundance data to find proteins with significant thermal stability shifts upon treatment.
- pitfalls: Using theoretical degrees of freedom (dfType = "theoretical") assumes independent and identically distributed (iid) residuals, which is violated due to the correlated nature of temperature measurements. This leads to anti-conservative p-values (overestimating significance). Use dfType = "empirical" instead. Failing to filter for complete curves (measurements at all temperatures across replicates and treatment groups) can bias or break the model fitting.

workflows.name: nparc_tpp_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform non-parametric analysis of response curves on TPP data to identify significantly shifted proteins.
input: stauro_TPP_data_tidy (tidy data frame containing columns for protein ID, temperature, relative abundance, compound concentration, and replicate)
workflows.stages: 1. Filter data for complete curves (all temperatures present in all replicates/groups) ;; 2. Fit null and alternative sigmoid models using NPARCfit ;; 3. Compute F-statistics and p-values using NPARCtest with empirical degrees of freedom ;; 4. Filter for significantly shifted proteins based on adjusted p-values
workflows.code:
BPPARAM <- BiocParallel::SerialParam(progressbar = FALSE)

fits <- NPARCfit(x = df$temperature, 
                 y = df$relAbundance, 
                 id = df$uniqueID, 
                 groupsNull = NULL, 
                 groupsAlt = df$compoundConcentration, 
                 BPPARAM = BPPARAM,
                 returnModels = FALSE)

modelMetrics <- fits$metrics 
fStats <- NPARCtest(modelMetrics, dfType = "empirical")

topHits <- fStats %>% 
  filter(pAdj <= 0.01) %>%
  dplyr::select(id, fStat, pVal, pAdj) %>%
  arrange(-fStat)
